# nps_workshop_network_flow_rule (Resource)

The `nps_workshop_network_flow_rule` resource manages network flow rules.

You need the `read:rules` and `write:rules` permissions.

Changing match criteria or other non-key fields updates the existing rule. Changing `name` or `tag` replaces it. Terraform destroys the old rule first, so hosts have no rule until the new one is created. Set `create_before_destroy` if you're renaming the rule or moving it to another tag.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A network flow rule that denies outgoing connections from a specific process
# to a remote domain.
resource "nps_workshop_network_flow_rule" "block_spacemolt" {
  name      = "block-spacemolt"
  tag       = "global"
  action    = "DENY"
  direction = "OUTGOING"

  process_signing_ids = [
    "Q6L2SF6YDW:com.anthropic.claude-code",
  ]

  remote_domains = [
    "spacemolt.com",
  ]

  comment = "Block claude-code from reaching spacemolt.com."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) The action to take on network flows matching this rule. The possible values are: `ALLOW`, `DENY`, `SILENT_DENY`, and `AUDIT`. The `NETWORK_FLOW_RULE_ACTION_`-prefixed spellings are deprecated aliases accepted for backwards compatibility.
- `direction` (String) The direction of network flows this rule applies to, relative to the host. The possible values are: `ANY`, `OUTGOING`, and `INCOMING`. The `NETWORK_FLOW_DIRECTION_`-prefixed spellings are deprecated aliases accepted for backwards compatibility.
- `name` (String) The name for this network flow rule. Rule names are unique per-tag.
- `tag` (String) The tag for this network flow rule. The tag determines which hosts this rule will apply to. The tag must already exist in Workshop.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) A comment to add to this rule. Will be displayed in the Workshop UI.
- `custom_msg` (String) A custom message to display to the user when this rule blocks a network flow.
- `custom_url` (String) A custom URL to redirect the user to when this rule blocks a network flow.
- `ports` (Block List) Port ranges that this rule applies to. An empty list matches any port. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--ports))
- `priority` (Boolean) If true, this rule wins over all ranked rules. Mutually exclusive with `rank`.
- `process_cd_hashes` (List of String) Process CDHashes that this rule applies to.
- `process_signing_ids` (List of String) Process signing IDs that this rule applies to.
- `process_team_ids` (List of String) Process team IDs that this rule applies to.
- `protocols` (List of Number) IANA protocol numbers (0-255) that this rule applies to. An empty list matches any protocol.
- `rank` (Number) The precedence rank for this rule. A higher rank wins over lower-ranked rules. Mutually exclusive with `priority`. When neither is set the effective rank is `0`.
- `remote_addresses` (List of String) Remote addresses that this rule applies to.
- `remote_domains` (List of String) Remote domains that this rule applies to.
- `remote_hostnames` (List of String) Remote hostnames that this rule applies to.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The server-generated ID of this network flow rule. This ID is reassigned on every upsert, including in-place updates, so it must not be relied on as a stable identifier across applies.

<a id="nestedblock--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ports`

Required:

- `low` (Number) The inclusive lower bound of the port range.

Optional:

- `high` (Number) The inclusive upper bound of the port range. Leave unset (or `0`) to match only the `low` port.

## Import

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import nps_workshop_network_flow_rule.block_spacemolt 12345
```
